4. PROLAPSE - one or more organs in the pelvis slip down from their normal position and bulge into the vagina.

Vaginal prolapse
Cervical prolapse
Uterine prolapse

Management of prolapse:
a) Replacement of the prolapse.
b) Apply salt or sugar solution to reduce swelling.
c) Suture the vulva if necessary.
d) Give anti-inflammatory drugs and antibiotics.

facts: Oxytocin (e.g., Oxytocin Bio 5 IU/ml injection solution) is used as a hormonal treatment for conditions such as retained placenta.
A mechanical approach can be utilized for addressing retained placenta.
Prolapse is defined as the condition where one or more organs in the pelvis slip down from their normal position and bulge into the vagina.
Common types of prolapse shown include vaginal prolapse, cervical prolapse, and uterine prolapse.
Step a in the management of prolapse is the replacement of the prolapse (repositioning the organ).
Step b in the management of prolapse is the application of a salt or sugar solution to reduce tissue swelling/edema.
Step c in the management of prolapse is suturing the vulva if necessary (retention sutures).
Step d in the management of prolapse includes administering anti-inflammatory drugs and antibiotics.
This content is part of the 'Dairysquare - Dairy Farming Module' on Page 55.
